analysis: All 14 units are test-only changes under provider-swift/Tests. They cover CLI status output (StatusResidencyTests.swift, new test at lines 119-176), test hooks in AutopilotPlacementFixture.swift (setAutopilotResidentSinceForTesting and setAutopilotLeaseForTesting at lines 120-126), new selected-model recovery fixtures, and new policy tests for SelectedModelPlacementPolicyTests and SelectedModelRecoveryPolicyTests. None of this is production code, so the PR adds no runtime attack surface. The new test hooks sit in an extension of ProviderLoop that is only reachable through @testable import ProviderCore. The tests write only to temporary sandbox directories and use stub engines, so they touch no real keys, credentials or consumer data. The retained tests do cover residency and eviction policy: Autopilot adoption holds are always honored, operator-selected models are never evicted while they are in the running daemon's selection, and recovery pauses while a drain, switch, load, or a live Autopilot lease is active. These behaviors bear on the availability and routing assumptions in TB-002 and TB-007 (T-010, T-029). I saw only the tests, not the production implementation. The production changes that these tests exercise (checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue, release of expired adoptions, eviction rules) are outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should review that code for races between request admission and release, for hold-expiry handling, and for any unadvertised model that could still receive requests after release. This batch gives no basis for a finding.
